articles.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
articles.summary: California’s attorney general and three city attorneys announced a $272.5 million settlement with Lyft after allegations that the company “committed wage theft by misclassifying drivers as independent contractors rather than employees” between 2016 and 2020, according to a Thursday statement . The case dates back to May 2020, when then-Attorney General Xavier Becerra, who is now the Democratic candidate for governor, sued both Uber and Lyft . That lawsuit said the ridehailing companies evaded state law when they declared that their drivers were not employees. Thursday’s settlement affects only Lyft, while the case against Uber continues. articles.title: These 9 Thunderbird features made me ditch Gmail for good
articles.summary: At the beginning of this year, I decided to ditch Gmail for the first time in about 15 years. It was not my plan to let down Google’s email app, as I have always enjoyed features such as Proofread, Confidential Mode, and Undo Send ( this one saved me once when I almost sent an email meant for my wife to my boss). But that does not mean it’s the best option for everyone. Over time, the Gmail app stopped feeling like a tool for sending and receiving emails and became like a marketer trying to sell me Google’s services. From the push for smart features that I don’t need to ads and the cluttered, AI-supported interface, checking my emails became a chore.

articles.title: I used Pixel’s new battery summaries for a week — and Google has work to do
articles.summary: I rolled my eyes when I heard Google was bringing AI battery summaries to Pixel phones. I’ve enjoyed some of the latest Gemini Intelligence improvements on my Pixel 11 Pro XL , but some implementations seem excessive. Still, battery life is a huge concern for many Pixel owners, so any new (and hopefully helpful) ways to analyze battery usage could have potential upsides. I tracked my battery usage for a week using Google’s new summary tool. In many ways, I wasn’t surprised, and it would be easy to throw battery summaries on the extensive pile of Google tools and features that shouldn’t exist. Still, there are some silver linings, and with a few tweaks, battery summaries can change how you manage your battery.

articles.title: I hate when Android brands copy Apple — but the iPhone Duo is the exception
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo is no longer a dream . Apple officially unveiled its first foldable iPhone at its September launch event, and while we’ll have to wait until later this month to actually get our hands on one, Apple entering a new category with a particular direction in mind usually means one thing: Android brands are about to follow. I’ve been pretty critical of Android OEMs over the past few years for blindly copying Apple’s strategies and bringing them to their own products. It often makes Android phones feel less interesting, less innovative, and, to be honest, sometimes just annoying.

articles.title: My Samsung phone was full of screenshots. This quick trick fixed it
articles.summary: I use the RegiStar Good Lock module to turn my Samsung phone’s backside into a virtual button. I’ve set up the double- and triple-tap gestures on my Galaxy S26 Ultra to take screenshots and toggle the privacy display feature, respectively. Although the former makes taking screenshots much easier than pressing button combinations, there’s one problem: sometimes, when I rotate the phone or switch it in my hands, the gesture accidentally gets triggered and takes a screenshot. Because of this, I end up with way too many unwanted screenshots in my gallery and need to delete them manually to prevent them from hogging space.

articles.title: The dawn of the age of the exoskeleton
articles.summary: This year, members of Seattle Mountain Rescue have been setting off into the wilds of the US Pacific Northwest wearing an unusual piece of kit . They’ve been hiking into the wilderness with powered assistive devices attached to their hips and legs. Designed to increase lower-body strength when climbing or carrying heavy loads, these pieces of equipment are being tested to see if they can boost rescuers’ speed and endurance when it matters most—during searches for stranded people. Devices like these are called human exoskeletons . They attach to parts of the body to create an external—or “exo”—mechanical structure. This powered frame enhances the wearer’s physical capabilities. Read full article Comments
